A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BYOL-γ research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renaming, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original OGBench evaluations, representation visualizations, ablations and horizon-generalization experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds recurrent-BYOL comparisons, full Forward-Backward experiments, a latent-dimension ablation and additional representation visualizations.

M1.justification: The proposed BYOL-γ procedure retains geometric future-state sampling, action-conditioned forward prediction, backward prediction, the representation losses and auxiliary BC training. v1's fixed-policy FB auxiliary objective is renamed TD-SR. The new recurrent-BYOL and full-FB procedures are comparison methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same OGBench navigation, antsoccer and visual tasks, including giant-maze horizon tests. The new appendix experiments revisit existing environments; recurrent prediction and fixed latent dimensions change configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 add action-conditioned recurrent BYOL with n = 1, 3 and 5, and a separate full Forward-Backward algorithm that learns a policy through RL. This full-FB comparator differs from v1's fixed-policy FB auxiliary loss, which remains as TD-SR.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce recurrent prediction lengths, a constant 64-dimensional latent-space control and a three-value learning-rate sweep for full FB. These are additional settings, rather than replacements for the retained benchmark protocol. Main training budgets, success metrics, evaluation tasks and checkpoint averaging remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 tests recurrent multi-step prediction and jointly removing backward prediction and discounting. Appendix B.4 tests sensitivity to encoder output dimension. Appendix G adds similarity maps for three existing environments. The original component, action-conditioning and horizon analyses remain.

E5.justification: Retained benchmarks still report means and standard deviations over 10 non-visual or four visual seeds, and retained component ablations use four seeds. The new recurrent-BYOL and full-FB comparisons also use four seeds. No new uncertainty estimator or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark and ablation tables have unchanged numerical entries. New Table 6 reports recurrent-BYOL averages of 28, 23 and 20 for n = 1, 3 and 5; Table 7 reports a full-FB average of 17. Table 8 adds fixed-dimension results, and Figure 6 adds qualitative findings. These are additional results, not improved scores for the original settings.

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives mixed-policy transition and successor quantities and a contrastive factorization, summarized in Table 1; v1 only discussed parts of this mismatch qualitatively. Appendix C also removes the unit-normalization assumption and changes the Taylor approximation's quadratic coefficient. Theorem 4.1 and its Appendix D proof are substantially retained.

C1.justification: v2 expands the central contribution from BYOL-γ and its successor-representation connection to a unified comparison of four objectives under single-policy and mixed-policy data. It also explicitly claims first use of TD-SR as a BC auxiliary loss. The original BYOL-γ contribution and empirical competitiveness claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes BYOL-γ's mixture of successor representations from TD-SR's successor representation of the mixture policy. It develops v1's pessimism hypothesis through within-policy positive and across-policy negative sampling, and discusses batch-computation tradeoffs and recurrent prediction's horizon constraints. The existing giant-maze and visual-task limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the recurrent prediction loss and full-FB implementation, including latent-vector sampling, BC regularization coefficient, architecture source and learning-rate sweep. It also specifies the 29/69-dimensional state encodings and 64-dimensional control. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware, runtime and code-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 removes the visual-pretraining discussion and its DynaMo, visual-cortex, R3M and masked-pretraining citations. It adds world-model and full-FB-related sources, including Richens, Lillicrap, Tirinzoni, and Touati and Ollivier, and introduces a TD-SR auxiliary-BC priority claim. The principal relationship to TRA and BYOL research remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and latter introduction are substantially rewritten, the contribution bullets are replaced, the background objectives are reordered, and Section 4.2 is reorganized around the comparative framework. The visual-pretraining subsection disappears, terminology changes from FB to TD-SR, and citations switch to author–year style.

P2.justification: v2 adds the objective-comparison table, three experimental tables, an encoder-architecture diagram and a multi-environment representation figure. Figure 2 gains a color scale. Existing tables and figures are resized or repositioned, including a side-caption ablation table; the horizon appendix is relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The recurrent-BYOL, full-FB and fixed-dimension comparisons address missing alternatives and controls in v1, strengthening empirical support and clarifying the baseline distinction. The theoretical benefit is limited by new Appendix E errors: Equations (30)/(33) use discount powers inconsistent with Section 3's normalization, and the quadratic derivation in (39)–(40) is inconsistent as written. These defects temper the otherwise useful additions.
